reasons: Correctly identifies the deviation: Section 11 selects Arizona law (outside the accepted NY/DE/CA/E&W set) and Sections 19 mandates binding arbitration instead of a court forum, so a deviation finding is warranted.

Redline reaches the preferred position exactly: 'laws of the Arizona' becomes 'laws of the State of New York' with the rest of the severability/governing-law sentence untouched, and the dispute clause now grants exclusive jurisdiction to the state and federal courts in New York County.

Removal of the arbitration mechanics (and the award-confirmation sentence) plus the retitle to 'Dispute Resolution' is a necessary consequence of moving to a court forum, so the high changed-character ratios on p0053/p0056 are justified rather than gratuitous rewriting; no substantive non-forum language was altered.
Comment is accurate, concise, first-person plural, prefixed, cites the playbook position and offers the Delaware/California/England-and-Wales fallback.
Severity held at medium is appropriate because the arbitration is domestic (U.S. Arbitration & Mediation), not seated abroad, so the walk-away trigger is not met.

Minor residual risk to confirm: the clause retains 'Except as otherwise specified below' and any unseen subparagraphs (a)-(c) or later carve-outs referencing 'the arbitrator' should be conformed so no orphan arbitration references remain.
